newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GM HUNGARY RESUME ENGINE OUTPUT AFTER SPAIN STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: GM HUNGARY RESUME ENGINE OUTPUT AFTER SPAIN STRIKE.

text.p: Engine production at the Hungarian plant of German automaker Adam Opel AG, a subsidiary of the U.S. General Motors will resume on Monday after a three-day stoppage caused by the now-resolved Spanish truckers' strike, the company said on Friday.
Output was halted on Wednesday due to lack of components from factories in Spain which could not deliver because of a two-week blockade by the lorry drivers.
The drivers went back to work on Thursday after the Spanish the government met some, but not all, of their demands.
"Production will start again on Monday and we hope to be back to normal production by Tuesday as the components arrive," Opel Hungary Ltd spokesman Zoltan Kaszas told Reuters.
Kaszas said the car assembly operation of Opel Astras and the company's cylinder head plant had not been affected.
The engine plant produces 1,700 1.4 litre and 1.6 litre Ecotec engines a day, which are exported to GM's car assembly plants around the world.
Kaszas said lost production, amounting to 5,000 units, would be made up through overtime and Saturday working.
Opel Hungary Ltd, launched in 1992, inaugurated last September new operations that double its engine production capacity to 460,000 units a year.

Along with the increase in engine production the company decided last year to reduce its car output to 11,100 units in 1996 from 12,488 units the year before, due to continuing adverse effects of the Hungarian government's austerity program on the country's car market.
Since it opened in 1992, Opel has invested over 700 million marks in its Hungarian operation.
